The Chaulukya page: 'Kumarapala captured Malwa from Ballala, who was killed by Kumarapala's Arbuda Paramara feudatory Yashodhavala'; his empire reached 'at least Vidisha (Bhilsa)'. Counterpart changed from the free text 'Ballala (usurper)' to 'nobody' (reviewer, 2026-10-19): Ballala is a usurper named once, not a state; the Paramara page has him 'the king of Dhara in the 1160 Veraval inscription', 'a former Paramara feudatory, a Hoysala chief, or a governor installed by the Chalukyas of Kalyani' (Jayavarman I page), so Malwa is unattributed land from 1143 to 1150.

Arbuda (Mount Abu), the Paramara chiefs' country

region.text: the northern marches of the Chaulukya kingdom: Naddula (Nadol) and the foot of Mount Abu, where the Ghurids marched in 1178

ledger.note: 1178: the Ghurids invade the Chaulukya kingdom. 'the Ghurid king Muhammad of Ghor invaded the Chaulukya kingdom in 1178 CE' (Chaulukya page); he had 'crossed the Indus River through the Gumal Pass ... capturing Multan and Uch' in 1175, then marched 'by the way of lower Sindh to penetrate into northern territory of the Chaulukyas'.

region.text: the Paramara kingdom of Malwa, Dhara and the country east to Vidisha (Bhilsa)

ledger.note: c. 1175-1178: Vindhyavarman takes Malwa back for the Paramaras. R. C. Majumdar dates the recovery to Mularaja II's reign (c. 1175-1178); A. K. Majumdar holds that 'Malwa remained under Chaulukya control during Mularaja's reign'; Dhara was Paramara 'by 1192'. Entered as the Chaulukya loss (this event is the Paramara dossier's gain).

union.text: Naddula (Nadol), the Chahamana feudatories' country in Marwar
Arbuda (Mount Abu), the Paramara chiefs' country

region.text: Naddula (Nadol) and the foot of Mount Abu

ledger.note: 1178: the Battle of Kasahrada. 'Kasahrada in Sirohi district near Mount Abu': 'the Ghurid forces were signally defeated' by Mularaja II with 'feudatories from Naddula, Jalor and Abu'; Muhammad 'sacked Nadol' and 'retreated back to his capital Ghazna', and 'Kelhanadeva managed to regain control of Naddula after the victory'. No land changed hands.

region.text: Naddula (Nadol), the Chahamana feudatories' country in Marwar

ledger.note: 1197: Aibak invades Naddula and the Naddula Chahamana line ends. 'In 1197 CE, the Ghurid general Qutb al-Din Aibak invaded Naddula and surrounding regions'; Jayatasimha, the last ruler, was 'probably defeated by the Ghurid Empire general Qutb al-Din Aibak in 1197 CE' and 'the Naddula kingdom disintegrated into several principalities'. Replaces the 1304 bridge (confidence 1) of the first version; Kirtipala 'established the Chahamana principality at Jalore' (no year).

region.text: Anahilavada (modern Patan), where Mularaja supplanted the last Chavda ruler

ledger.note: 4 February 1197: Aibak takes Anahilapataka. 'On 4 February 1197 CE, the Ghurid general Qutb al-Din Aibak invaded Bhima's capital Anahilapataka, and inflicted a massive defeat on the Chaulukyas.' Held without annexing the kingdom: hatched over the capital district.

region.text: Anahilavada (modern Patan), where Mularaja supplanted the last Chavda ruler

ledger.note: By 1201: the capital is Chaulukya again. 'the capital was back under the Chaulukya rule by 1201 CE' after Lavanaprasada and Shridhara 'forced the Ghurids to retreat'.

region.text: Mewar (Medapata): the 60 cells of the Cliopatria shape in the Guhila homeland

ledger.note: 1213 (bridge): the Guhilas of Medapata break away. "The Guhilas of Medapata ... also rebelled against Bhima sometime between 1207 and 1227 CE, and declared their independence." The page gives no year inside the window; 1213 is the first year of Jaitrasimha's reign in the Guhila dossier (Guhila dynasty page: r. c. 1213-1252, 'the Guhilas achieved a high political status'), which draws Mewar as Guhila from that year. Mirror of guhilas-of-mewar ledger 3. Bhima 'managed to regain control of the throne during 1223-1226 CE' but the page names no recovery of Mewar.

region.text: Arbuda (Mount Abu), the Paramara chiefs' country

ledger.note: c. 1220 (bridge): the Abu Paramara line ends. Paramaras of Chandravati page: Dharavarsha 'ruled as a Chaulukya feudatory', his 'last inscription dated 1219 CE (1276 VS)', reign table 'c. 1160-1220' and 'the last known ruler of dynasty'; infobox 'Disestablished: c. 13th century CE'. The page does not say the vassalage ended; it replaces the first version's 1304 (confidence 1).

region.text: the Lata region, southern Gujarat

ledger.note: 1220: the Yadava Simhana invades Lata. Seuna page: 'killed the defending ruler Simha, and captured Lata'; the Chaulukya page: 'the Yadavas invaded the southern part of the Chaulukya kingdom, led by Bhillama's successors Jaitugi and Simhana' (no year); Lavanaprasada and Viradhavala 'warded off the Yadava invasions'. Seuna page (reread 2026-10-19): 'In 1220, Simhana sent an army to the Lata region in present-day Gujarat'; Kholeshvara 'killed the Lata ruler Simha and captured Lata' (no year); 'Simha's son Shankha was appointed Yadava vassal in Lata'; 'Lavanaprasada later invaded Lata and captured Khambhat'. Lata proper was not in the Chaulukya shape in 1220 (lost 1077), so no Chaulukya loss is entered; the contest keeps the zone fought over (the whole Lata region, with the northern margin the Chaulukyas held).

region.text: the Lata region, southern Gujarat

ledger.note: c. 1232: peace with the Yadavas. Seuna page: 'The Chaulukya-Yadava conflict came to end in c. 1232 with a peace treaty.'

c. 1244: Visaladeva founds the Vaghela dynasty. 'Visaladeva ascended the throne of Gujarat sometime around 1244 CE'; the Chaulukya page: 'After Tribhuvanapala, they seized the throne, establishing the Vaghela dynasty' (the Vaghelas 'had earlier served as Chaulukya generals' and claimed descent from a sister of Kumarapala). Same state and colour (rule 2): the Vaghelas rule the same Gujarat kingdom.

region.text: Gujarat

ledger.note: 1299: Alauddin Khalji's army ransacks Gujarat. 'In 1299, the Delhi Sultan Alauddin Khalji sent an army to ransack Gujarat.'

region.text: Gujarat

ledger.note: 1304: the second Delhi invasion ends the contest. 'In 1304, Karna lost his throne permanently after a second invasion from Delhi.' (The page names Nusrat Khan.)

region.text: Gujarat

ledger.note: 1304: Gujarat goes to Delhi. 'Karna lost his throne permanently after a second invasion from Delhi.' The page gives the end of the Vaghelas as 1304 ('Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Gujarat').

region.text: Gujarat, Saurashtra and Kutch

ledger.note: 1304: the Chaulukya-Vaghela kingdom of Gujarat ends. Cliopatria's row ends in 1249; the Chaulukyas as such end in c. 1244 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1244 CE').

wars.name: Chaulukya-Paramara wars (Malwa)

zones.text: the Paramara kingdom of Malwa, Dhara and the country east to Vidisha (Bhilsa)

wars.outcome: Jayasimha took Dhara in 1135-1136; Jayavarman I regained it 1142-1143; Ballala held it until Kumarapala's victory c. 1150; Vindhyavarman restored Paramara rule c. 1175-1178 (by 1192 at the latest).

wars.name: Ghaznavid raid on Somnath
wars.outcome: 'the Ghaznavid ruler Mahmud invaded the kingdom and raided the Somnath temple during 1024-1025 CE'; Bhima fled to Kanthkot and Mahmud 'entered the Chaulukya territory unopposed'. A raid without annexation.

wars.name: Chaulukya-Kalachuri war for Lata

zones.text: Lata proper, southern Gujarat: the Vadodara and Surat discs without the northern margin (59 cells at 21.2-23.4 N, 72.1-73.7 E) that Cliopatria's 1111-1303 Chaulukya shapes keep and that lies in Gujarat proper

wars.outcome: The Kalachuris (general Vapullaka) took Lata after Bhoja's death in 1055; Karna evicted them by 1074 and lost it to Trivikramapala within three years. Recorded in the ledger as a Paramara loss (1056), a Chaulukya gain (1074) and loss (1077).

wars.name: Naddula Chahamana invasion under Karna
wars.outcome: Prithvipala 'defeated Karna', and Jojalladeva 'occupied the Chaulukya capital Anahilapataka, possibly when Karna was busy at another place'. The page gives no year.

wars.outcome: Muhammad of Ghor reached Mount Abu and was beaten at Kasahrada in 1178; Aibak defeated Bhima II and sacked Anahilapataka on 4 February 1197; the capital was Chaulukya again by 1201.

wars.name: Battle of Kasahrada
wars.outcome: Chaulukya victory over Muhammad of Ghor at Kasahrada near Mount Abu; he retreated to Ghazna; no territorial change.

wars.name: Chaulukya-Chahamana war
wars.outcome: Prithviraja III 'invaded Gujarat but could not gain much success and concluded a peace treaty with Chaulukya Bhima II' (before 1187, Prithviraj page); the Chaulukya page names Jagaddeva as the negotiator.

wars.name: Yadava invasions of Lata
wars.outcome: Simhana captured Lata in 1220 and installed a vassal; peace c. 1232.

wars.name: Delhi Sultanate conquest of Gujarat
wars.outcome: Ransacked in 1299; Karna lost his throne permanently in 1304.

certainty.note: No treaty line is given on any page opened; the limits are the reach of inscriptions and of feudatories (Naddula, Jalor, Abu, Chudasama Saurashtra). The peace with Prithviraja III (before 1187) and the Yadava peace (c. 1232) fix no line.

notes:
Settled from pages: founding c. 940, Malwa annexed 1135-1136 and lost c. 1175-1178 (Paramara pages), Lata's owners (see the repair paragraph), the Ghurid defeat of 1178, the 1197-1201 Ghurid hold of the capital, the Vaghela dynasty from c. 1244 and the end in 1304.
Decision: the Vaghelas are treated as a dynasty change inside this state (rule 2; Cliopatria's Chaulukya row runs to 1249, the Vaghelas 'had earlier served as Chaulukya generals' and claimed descent from a sister of Kumarapala). The dossier therefore ends in 1304, not 1244, and a keyframe 1250-1304 extends the 1241 shape. If another group writes a vaghela-dynasty dossier it should be merged here or given a new state colour deliberately.
Not settled: (1) The Chaulukya reign table on the Chaulukya page is garbled (Kumarapala's accession is printed 1043, a typo for 1143), so no ruler list is given. (2) The Naddula Chahamana occupation of the capital by Jojalladeva is undated and not drawn. (3) Dates of the Chudasama/Saurashtra conquests are not given; Saurashtra stays in the shape on the strength of 'Mularaja defeated Graharipu' and Kumarapala's 'Kachchha and Saurashtra'; the Chudasamas need a dossier as local rulers (vassal tint). (4) Cliopatria moves 67 Lata cells to the Western Chalukyas in 1111; no page dates it. (5) The Guhilas of Medapata (Mewar, 60 cells) rebelled 1207-1227 and are not subtracted. (6) The 1031 start of the Abu vassalage is the Bhoja page's date for Bhima's expedition. (7) Counterparts without a dossier: chavda-dynasty, chalukyas-of-lata, kalachuris-of-tripuri, paramaras-of-chandravati, chahamanas-of-naddula, Trivikramapala, Ballala (usurper). Gazetteer names needed: Anahilapataka (Patan, 23.85 N 72.12 E), Nadol (25.37 N 73.58 E), Mount Abu (24.59 N 72.71 E). Pages (5): Chaulukya dynasty (opened twice), Jayasimha Siddharaja, Battle of Kasahrada, Vaghela dynasty, Paramara dynasty; Seuna, Vindhyavarman, Bhoja and Prithviraj Chauhan were opened for other dossiers and cited here.

Repair 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review of sa-03-f, verdict fail). (1) Lata: one timeline for chaulukya-dynasty, paramara-dynasty and western-chalukya-empire, with one region, Lata proper (the Vadodara 120 km and Surat 80 km discs minus the 59 northern-margin cells of Cliopatria's 1111 Chaulukya shape, which lie in Gujarat proper): Chaulukya suzerainty to 1006; Kalyani Chalukyas by 1007; Chaulukya 1008 (Durlabharaja, confidence 1); Kirtiraja of the Lata Chalukyas from 1009; Paramara 1018-1055; Kalachuris 1056-1073 (Karna page: the general Vapullaka); Chaulukya 1074-1076 (Karna: 'By 1074 CE'); Trivikramapala from 1077; Cliopatria's 1111 shape gives the southern cells to the Western Chalukyas. The first version had Lata Chaulukya 1008-1063 and 1074-1304, which overlapped the Paramara 1018-1055 claim. The 1064 loss (confidence 1) was removed. I disagree with the review only in the region: the reviewer measured with the whole 206-cell disc union; its northern 59 cells are Gujarat proper and the Chaulukya shape keeps them from 1111 to 1303 without an event, so the Lata events use Lata proper (147 cells). (2) The 1111 shape now has bridges (confidence 1): +31 cells from Paramara, +17 from the Soomras (Cliopatria's Sind-Habbari 1110 shape), +192 from nobody, -35 to nobody. (3) 942, not 947, for Gujarat and Kutch, counterpart gurjara-pratihara-dynasty, as the Pratihara dossier (/ledger/27) has it; Saurashtra stays at 947 (counterpart chavda-dynasty); the found event stays at c. 940 (Chaulukya page; the Mularaja page gives 940-941, the Chavda page 942). (4) 'Ballala (usurper)' and 'Trivikramapala' became 'nobody' with the names in the notes. (5) Thin items looked at: Abu vassalage now ends c. 1220 (Paramaras of Chandravati page: last ruler Dharavarsha, last inscription 1219; confidence 1) and the Naddula vassalage in 1197 (Aibak's invasion, confidence 2), instead of 1304; the Guhila page gives no year for the Mewar revolt of 1207-1227, so the Mewar cells stay; the Vaghela page gives no extent for 1250-1304; the Seuna page's 'captured Lata' (Kholeshvara, no year) is a Lata proper event, not a Chaulukya loss. Still open: the 1136-1150 Malwa dates, the Saurashtra/Kutch conquests (undated), the Chudasamas. Counterparts needing a dossier: chavda-dynasty, chalukyas-of-lata, kalachuris-of-tripuri, paramaras-of-chandravati, chahamanas-of-naddula; kachchhapaghatas are not used here.
